title: Admin Webhook DLQ router is double-prefixed (/api/v1/api/v1/...) — list / detail / replay all 404 despite being mounted
reason: Independently confirmed via the request-path mechanics. webhook-dlq.hono.ts:59,89,115 register ABSOLUTE literals app.get('/api/v1/webhooks/dead-letters'), '/.../:id', app.post('/.../:id/replay') — it is the ONLY router in routes/*.hono.ts using /api/v1 absolute paths (grep confirms all others use relative). Mounted via api.route('/', webhookDlqRouter) at index.ts:1736 onto the Hono `api` instance (index.ts:1153 const api = new Hono()), which is served by Express via app.use('/api/v1', handle(api)) at index.ts:1862 (app = express() at 624, handle from '@hono/node-server/vercel' at 48). Verified handle() → getRequestListener(app.fetch); newRequest() reads incoming.url (node_modules/@hono/node-server/dist/vercel.js:188-218, 'const incomingUrl = incoming.url'). Express mountpath stripping rewrites req.url to the unmounted remainder, so Hono receives '/webhooks/dead-letters', never matching the registered '/api/v1/webhooks/dead-letters' → 404. FE client WebhookDLQClient.tsx:39,54,66 calls relative '/webhooks/dead-letters*' (base /api/v1) → composed /api/v1/webhooks/dead-letters → strip → /webhooks/dead-letters → no match. The isolation test webhook-dlq-router.test.ts:114 calls app.request('/api/v1/webhooks/dead-letters') directly on the un-mounted router (no Express stripping) so it passes and masks the bug. Nav-linked at StaffNav.tsx:49 href '/webhook-dlq'. admin-platform-portal is canonical (docker-compose.production.yml:447). Not in KNOWN_ISSUES.
userImpact: The nav-linked Webhook DLQ admin page always 404s. Operators cannot list, inspect, or replay any dead-lettered webhook delivery — at-least-once webhook recovery is operationally inaccessible.
proposedFix: Change the route literals in webhook-dlq.hono.ts to relative paths ('/webhooks/dead-letters', '/webhooks/dead-letters/:id', '/webhooks/dead-letters/:id/replay'), OR mount via api.route('/webhooks/dead-letters', …) with stripped literals. title: Stripe payment webhook has no durable idempotency claim — concurrent redelivery can double-credit the ledger
reason: Independently confirmed and reachable in the shipped standalone server (server.ts app.listen at :2259; Stripe posts webhooks directly here). The /webhooks/stripe handler (server.ts:1432-1511) never calls webhookIdempotencyStore.claim(), whereas the STK path (server.ts:1561) and C2B path (server.ts:1807) do. payment_intent.succeeded → handleWebhook → handlePaymentSuccess → bookPaymentToLedger, which does a check-then-act guard (findEntriesByPaymentIntent, orchestration:492-502, existing.length>0 skip) and then postJournalEntry at orchestration:552 with NO options/idempotencyKey. The DB index is non-unique: packages/database/src/schemas/ledger.schema.ts:214 declares index('ledger_entries_payment_intent_idx'), not a unique constraint, so nothing serializes two concurrent first-posts. Not in KNOWN_ISSUES: KI-012 is specifically about the M-Pesa idempotency CACHE being process-local (in-process LRUCache vs Redis), a different defect on a different (M-Pesa) path — it does not cover the Stripe route lacking any claim and bookPaymentToLedger lacking an engine-level key.
userImpact: On concurrent Stripe payment_intent.succeeded redelivery (Stripe parallel retry, or two app replicas), a customer's rent payment can be booked twice — customer-liability double-reduced, holding double-credited — corrupting balances and over-stating disbursable funds.
proposedFix: Wrap the Stripe webhook in the same webhookIdempotencyStore.claim/release pattern the M-Pesa paths use, keyed by tenant+'stripe'+event.id; AND pass { idempotencyKey: `payment:${paymentIntent.id}` } into postJournalEntry inside bookPaymentToLedger (orchestration:552) so engine-level dedupe protects every booking path. Optionally add a unique index on (tenant_id, payment_intent_id) for the rent-payment journal as a DB-level backstop.

title: M-Pesa B2C disbursement is unreachable (provider never registered) and its result/timeout callbacks are no-op stubs
reason: Confirmed. disbursementService.registerProvider is called ONLY with stripeProvider (server.ts:444); mpesaProvider is registered only with paymentOrchestrationService (server.ts:457), never with disbursementService. getProvider() (disbursement.service.ts:602-611) returns this.providers.get(this.defaultProvider) — always the default (Stripe), never currency/market-selected — so processDisbursement (reachable via route at server.ts:1289) always calls Stripe's createTransfer (disbursement.service.ts:259), and MpesaPaymentProvider.createTransfer (mpesa-provider.ts:362) is dead. The B2C callbacks are pure stubs: /webhooks/mpesa/b2c/result (server.ts:1667-1695) logs + acks ResultCode:0 with the literal comment 'In a full implementation, update the disbursement status', and /b2c/timeout (server.ts:1700-1711) likewise. getTransferStatus throws unconditionally (mpesa-provider.ts:444) and createTransfer returns status:'PENDING' (mpesa-provider.ts:436). The disbursement-reconciliation job filters status==='NEEDS_REVERSAL' (disbursement-reconciliation.job.ts:142), so a PENDING/PROCESSING B2C transfer is never examined. Not in KNOWN_ISSUES.
userImpact: Owners in mobile-money markets (TZ launch / KES) cannot be paid out via M-Pesa at all — only Stripe, which does not serve M-Pesa payouts. If the B2C path were wired, a failed payout would leave money debited from holding, never delivered, never reversed (callback no-op + status query throws + recon job ignores non-NEEDS_REVERSAL rows).
proposedFix: Register mpesaProvider with disbursementService and make getProvider() select by destination/currency rather than a single default. Implement /b2c/result to look up the disbursement by ConversationID and mark PAID, or transition to NEEDS_REVERSAL on failure so the recon job consumes it; implement /b2c/timeout to flag NEEDS_REVERSAL. Until wired, remove the dead B2C provider/callback surface so it cannot be mistaken for working.

title: Direct M-Pesa C2B paybill payment is silently dropped — no intent, no ledger booking, no 'unallocated' record
reason: Confirmed. The registered M-Pesa provider's name is the literal 'mpesa' (mpesa-provider.ts:99 `readonly name = 'mpesa'`), and intents record provider via aggregate.markProcessing(externalId, provider.name) (orchestration:326). The string 'mpesa_c2b' appears ONLY in the C2B confirm handler calling handleWebhook('mpesa_c2b', c2b.TransID, 'SUCCEEDED', ...) at server.ts:1815 and :1832 — no createPayment/processPayment path ever creates an intent with provider 'mpesa_c2b' and externalId=TransID. So handleWebhook's findByExternalId returns null and the method logs 'Payment intent not found' and returns (orchestration:638-645). The idempotency claim is held (server.ts:1807), so Daraja retries dedupe too. The 'lands in an unallocated bucket' text at server.ts:1829 is a comment only — no code creates an unallocated record or books anything. Not in KNOWN_ISSUES.
userImpact: Cash that genuinely arrived via M-Pesa C2B (customer pays the paybill directly, no app-initiated STK) is acked to Safaricom (ResultCode:0) but recorded nowhere — no ledger entry, no unallocated row, no operator task. The money is real, the record is absent: a silent revenue/attribution loss.
proposedFix: On a C2B confirmation with no matching intent, create a payment intent (or an explicit 'unallocated receipt' record) for the amount/MSISDN/TransID and book it to a holding/unallocated account via postJournalEntry (balanced) so operators can attribute it later — never ack-and-drop.

title: OAuth device-code /token endpoint mints multiple valid bearer tokens from one grant (TOCTOU, no transaction, no compare-and-swap)
reason: Independently confirmed reachable on the shipped public path. (1) POST /oauth/token is registered on publicApp (oauth-device.hono.ts:275), which mounts databaseMiddleware (line 154) but has NO authMiddleware, so auth/tenantId is undefined. (2) database.ts:515 `if (!database || useMockData || !tenantId) { await next(); return; }` short-circuits the tenant transaction — confirmed verbatim — so the handler runs with NO wrapping transaction. (3) The handler body (lines 294-348) is a bare read-then-write: SELECT row (294-298) -> assert row.status==='approved' (327) -> INSERT a fresh oauth_agent_tokens row with a freshly randomBytes(32) token (335-344) -> UPDATE status='consumed' WHERE deviceCode (345-348). The UPDATE is `where(eq(oauthDeviceCodes.deviceCode, row.deviceCode))` with NO `AND status='approved'` predicate — confirmed it is unconditional, not a compare-and-swap. No db.transaction() is opened inside the handler. (4) Migration 0282 (read in full) has no device_code column on oauth_agent_tokens and no unique constraint tying a token to a device_code/approval — only token_hash is unique, and each concurrent request generates a distinct random token, so both inserts succeed. (5) The only concurrency control is getSharedPublicAiRateLimit, a per-IP sliding window (20/window) that does not serialize per device_code and explicitly multiplies across replicas (public-ai-rate-limit.ts:24,254). RFC 8628 clients poll every ~5s with overlapping retries; two concurrent polls both read 'approved' and both mint a live, independently-revocable token. Not in KNOWN_ISSUES.md nor any Docs/AUDIT report.
userImpact: A single owner approval can yield 2+ live agent bearer tokens for the same client/device under overlapping polls (guaranteed with >1 gateway replica). The duplicate is a distinct row with its own id/revoked_at, so revoking the first does not revoke the second, and the connected-agents list (GET /oauth/agent-tokens) shows them only as separate active tokens — a token-duplication / lingering-credential vector on the agent-platform auth surface (Claude Code / Cursor / CLI / SDK). Both /token responses return 200 so nothing flags the double issuance. Severity lowered from blocker to high: exploitation requires a race window on an already-owner-approved grant (no privilege escalation, no cross-tenant access — both tokens carry the same tenant/user/scope), and the device_code is single-use on the happy path; impact is duplicate-credential / incomplete-revocation rather than unauthorized access.
proposedFix: Make the consume atomic with a single guarded UPDATE that only flips approved->consumed and returns the binding when it was still approved, e.g. `UPDATE oauth_device_codes SET status='consumed', consumed_at=now() WHERE device_code=$1 AND status='approved' RETURNING tenant_id, user_id, client_id, client_label, scopes`; insert the agent token ONLY when a row is returned, otherwise return authorization_pending/invalid_grant. Because databaseMiddleware does not open a transaction on this public path (database.ts:515), wrap the claim+insert in an explicit db.transaction() in the handler. Optionally add a partial unique index keying one active agent token per device_code/approval id as DB-level defense-in-depth.

title: Global ensureTenantIsolation middleware is a permanent no-op — documented 'FIXED H-2' defense-in-depth never fires, and cross-org denial telemetry is dark
reason: Independently confirmed. (1) ensureTenantIsolation is mounted exactly once, globally, at api.use('*', ensureTenantIsolation) (index.ts:1159) with the comment 'FIXED H-2 ... defense-in-depth'; grep shows it is never re-applied inside any router (only test files reference it). (2) Its guard is `if (auth && tenant && auth.tenantId !== tenant.id)` (tenant-context.middleware.ts:732). (3) The only production writers of c.set('tenant', ...) are tenant-context.middleware.ts:575 and :612, both inside tenantContextMiddleware / optionalTenantContextMiddleware. grep across services/ (excluding tests) shows NEITHER is mounted anywhere in production — tenantContextMiddleware appears only in test files (tz-tenant-e2e.test.ts, compliance-plugins.test.ts, test-user-isolation.test.ts, cross-tenant-isolation.test.ts). So c.get('tenant') is undefined on every real request. (4) authMiddleware is NOT applied at the global api.use level (it is mounted per-router); confirmed via grep that index.ts has no global authMiddleware mount, so at line 1159 c.get('auth') is also undefined. Both operands undefined => the guard at line 732 never evaluates true and control always falls through to await next(). (5) The crossOrgDenialRecorder call (lines 752-767) lives inside that unreachable TENANT_MISMATCH branch, so the cross-org denial telemetry the docstring calls 'the single highest-signal security event' is never recorded by this path. (6) database.ts:317-326 itself documents RLS is INERT under a BYPASSRLS Supabase role, so the only real backstop (RLS) can also be inert in that posture. Not in KNOWN_ISSUES.md nor any Docs/AUDIT report.
userImpact: The advertised second layer of cross-tenant isolation does not exist at runtime: with c.get('tenant') always undefined (and c.get('auth') undefined at the global mount point) the TENANT_MISMATCH 403 can never fire and never records a denial. Cross-tenant isolation rests entirely on per-handler scoping by auth.tenantId plus RLS — and RLS is documented as inert under the Supabase BYPASSRLS prod role (database.ts:317-326). Any router that forgets to scope a query by auth.tenantId has no backstop here despite the code/comment claiming one, and the brute-force pattern scanner that consumes crossOrgDenialRecorder output is starved of the cross-org denial signal.
proposedFix: Either (a) mount tenantContextMiddleware in production so c.get('tenant') is populated AND move ensureTenantIsolation to run AFTER per-router authMiddleware so c.get('auth') is set; or (b) rewrite ensureTenantIsolation to derive the request-tenant from a server-trusted post-auth source and compare against auth.tenantId, mounting it inside each tenant-scoped router group after authMiddleware. Re-home the crossOrgDenialRecorder call onto a path that actually executes on a cross-tenant attempt. Until one lands, remove the misleading 'FIXED H-2 / defense-in-depth' comment at index.ts:1157-1158 so the no-op is not mistaken for active protection.

title: proactive-triggers mark-seen BEFORE emit: a failed sink emit permanently suppresses the trigger, drops user-bound work with no staff alert, and is reported as 'fired'
reason: Confirmed at services/proactive-triggers-worker/src/schedule/cron-handler.ts. Line 151 deps.cache.markSeen(trigger.id, lookbackHours) executes BEFORE line 152 await safeEmit(...). safeEmit (179-200) catches any sink.emit failure and only logs a warn — it never rethrows and never un-marks. Line 153 triggersFired += 1 increments unconditionally after safeEmit returns. So a transient sink outage marks the trigger seen for the full lookback window (default 24h, from env LOOKBACK_HOURS), hasSeenRecently() suppresses it on the next sweep, and the summary counts it as fired. NOTE: this is reachable only once finding 2 is fixed (the worker currently never sweeps at all), but the ordering bug is a real, independently-correct defect in the sweep path.
fileLine: services/proactive-triggers-worker/src/schedule/cron-handler.ts:151-153 (markSeen, then safeEmit, then triggersFired++); 186-199 (safeEmit swallows failure with only a warn)
userImpact: When the notification sink is briefly down, the trigger is marked seen for the lookback window but the user never receives it; the next sweep suppresses it (lost for up to 24h or permanently). The sweep summary reports it as triggersFired, misleading operators, and no staff alert is raised for the dropped notification.
proposedFix: Emit first, then markSeen only on confirmed success: have safeEmit RETURN ok/failed; on failure do NOT markSeen (so the next sweep retries) and increment a triggersDropped counter that raises a staff alert when >0. Counting a trigger as fired must require a successful emit.

reason: Confirmed in both paths. On retry/redelivery recordEvent returns inserted:false and the system reports idempotent success though no billing line exists. fileLine: services/outcomes-metering/src/routes/events.ts:192-208,226 (anchor before billing line, non-transactional; duplicate returns 200 idempotent:true); services/outcomes-metering/src/consumers/brain-event-consumer.ts:217-227,241-251,257,283

title: sleep-pass-orchestrator runs replicas:2 (HPA→6) with no leader-election and no in-flight guard — breaks single-dispatch / ATOMIC-CLAIM when real adapters land
reason: Confirmed. infra/k8s/sleep-pass-orchestrator/base/deployment.yaml:18 replicas:2; hpa.yaml minReplicas:2 maxReplicas:6. orchestrator.ts start() (112-117) is setInterval(() => void tick(), intervalMs) with NO re-entrancy latch and NO timer.unref(); tick() (89-110) sets state.lastRunAt only AFTER each pass completes (line 100-105). There is no k8s Lease/leader-election in the manifest and no distributed claim. setInterval does not await the prior `void tick()`, so a tick exceeding 60s (dead-letter-replay maxDurationMs is 5min) overlaps the next. Note: proactive-triggers-worker's own manifest pins replicas:1 explicitly because 'multiple replicas would duplicate trigger fires absent leader-election' — the identical hazard is left unguarded here. Currently masked because passes run on in-memory per-pod adapters, but the structural defect is real and bites the instant shared-state adapters land.
userImpact: Each replica independently dispatches the same passes. Once shared-state adapters replace the in-memory ones, dead-letter-replay replays each DLQ message N times, index-maintenance runs concurrent REINDEX, expired-token-cleanup double-deletes, audit-chain-verify runs N times. In-process, a >60s tick can also double-run a pass on a single replica.
proposedFix: Pin the orchestrator to replicas:1 with Recreate strategy and drop the HPA, OR add k8s Lease-based leader election so only the leader ticks; add a per-process in-flight latch in start() (skip the callback if the previous tick is still running) plus timer.unref(). When prod adapters land, make each pass claim its work atomically (UPDATE..SET status='taken' WHERE status IN(dispatchable) RETURNING).

title: sleep-pass-orchestrator runs entirely on in-memory adapters in production — security/integrity passes silently do nothing
reason: Confirmed. services/sleep-pass-orchestrator/src/standalone-bootstrap.ts:89-102 wires all 9 passes to createInMemory*Adapter unconditionally; index.ts:124 main() calls buildStandaloneOrchestrator() and index.ts:136 calls bundle.orchestrator.start(). deployment.yaml runs NODE_ENV=production with SLEEP_PASS_PROD_ADAPTERS unset, so the fail-fast guard at standalone-bootstrap.ts:80 is NOT triggered and the orchestrator ticks against empty in-memory state. dead-letter-replay.ts:48 hardcodes errored:false even when the local errored counter (line 29/37) is >0 — only reflected in the notes string, never in the result.errored field. userImpact: In production every pass operates on empty in-memory adapters touching no real system: expired auth/reset tokens never cleaned, audit hash-chain never verified, dead-letter queue never replayed, dormant tenants never detected, indexes never maintained — while /healthz and /metrics report a healthy pod. dead-letter-replay additionally reports errored:false even when every replay failed, hiding the failure.

Make dead-letter-replay propagate errored:true and raise a staff alert when any replay fails. Add a readiness gate so a memory-mode orchestrator cannot pass readiness under NODE_ENV=production.

reason: Confirmed at services/api-gateway/src/routes/marketplace/listings.hono.ts:332-342: .limit(100) with no offset/cursor param accepted in the handler (lines 314-342 take no pagination input), and meta:{ total: rows.length }. issueClass: unbounded-then-truncated list read + meta.total computed as page length

title: AccountRepository.find() has no LIMIT — monthly statement cron and ledger-integrity check load the entire accounts table for a tenant
reason: Confirmed at drizzle-account.repository.ts:225-259: find(filters) builds a where clause and selects with orderBy but NO .limit() (lines 252-256). Reachable in shipped runtime: generateOwnerMonthlyStatements/generateCustomerMonthlyStatements call accountRepository.find({tenantId,type,status}) (statement-generation.job.ts:96-100,176-180) and are invoked from POST /api/v1/admin/jobs/statements (server.ts:1896-1897). verifyLedgerBalances calls find({tenantId}) (reconciliation.service.ts:411) and is invoked from POST /api/v1/reconciliation/run (server.ts:2187) and POST /api/v1/admin/jobs/reconciliation path. The N+1 in the verify path is also real: lines 422-427 loop calculateAccountBalance once per account. On large institutional tenants this materializes all accounts into memory and issues a per-account balance query. Not in KNOWN_ISSUES/audit.
issueClass: unbounded list read feeding a batch cron (heap pressure) + N+1
userImpact: On a tenant with tens of thousands of OWNER_OPERATING/CUSTOMER_LIABILITY accounts, the statement job loads the entire account set into worker memory before its serial loop (heap-pressure/OOM risk that aborts the whole monthly run). The verify path additionally issues one balance query per account (thousands-deep N+1) that can hold the run open for minutes and saturate the DB.
proposedFix: Add a bounded keyset-paged find variant ({ limit, afterId }) and iterate pages in the statement job and integrity check. For the integrity check, replace the per-account calculateAccountBalance N+1 with a single set-based query that computes all balances in one pass.

title: Kill-switch 'degraded' level is a silent no-op — the documented stakes restriction does not exist in any caller
reason: Independently confirmed. resolveKillswitch (killswitch.ts:184-198) returns {level:'degraded'} correctly, and parseLevel (killswitch.ts:130-143) deliberately FAILS CLOSED to 'degraded' for any unrecognized non-empty value (e.g. a typo'd 'halt'). But the kernel never acts on it: think() non-stream path only writes a trace line at kernel.ts:744-748 (`level=${ks.level} reason=...`) then proceeds at full capability; think$() stream path at kernel.ts:1807-1833 branches ONLY on ks.level==='halt' and never observes 'degraded'. Repo-wide grep for `ks.level === 'degraded'` / level==='degraded' as a stakes restriction returns ZERO consumers outside killswitch.ts's own resolution precedence — the `stakes` references in kernel.ts (debate/judge gating at 1129/1328/1393 etc.) branch only on req.stakes from the request and never cross-reference ks.level. The docstring at killswitch.ts:25-27 promises 'lower-stakes calls only / Mapped onto stakes filter in callers' — that mapping does not exist. Not in KNOWN_ISSUES.md (grep clean) nor audit-reports. The fail-closed parser is load-bearing here: it was written specifically so a typo degrades rather than runs live, but the degrade is a no-op, so a fat-fingered HALT serves sovereign actions fully live.
userImpact: An operator who sets KILLSWITCH_STATE=degraded (a compliance/incident soft-hold) — OR who fat-fingers a HALT directive into an unrecognized value that parseLevel fails closed to 'degraded' — believes brain capability is curtailed. In reality the kernel runs every turn, including high/critical-stakes sovereign actions (evictions, owner payouts, KRA filings), at full capability. The 'kill-switch fail-closed' hard rule is partially defeated for the degraded tier.
proposedFix: In both think() and think$(), after resolveKillswitch, branch on ks.level==='degraded' and refuse/escalate any req.stakes==='high'|'critical' turn (or force the most-cautious route and surface the degraded state in the decision, not just a trace line). At minimum gate critical-stakes side-effect routing behind a non-degraded check so a typo'd HALT cannot serve sovereign actions.

title: Sovereign-tier action ledger defaults to FAIL-OPEN — irreversible eviction/payout/KRA actions report success even when the hash-chained audit row fails to write
reason: Independently confirmed with one nuance. safeSovereignLedger (executor.ts:949) computes failClosed = (deps.sovereignLedgerFailClosed === true); on a ledger-write throw it returns {ok:true} (executor.ts:974) by default. readSovereignLedgerFailClosedFromEnv (service-registry.ts:3083-3096) defaults to false for undefined/null/empty. All three composition sites pass it through (sovereign.ts:380, sovereign.ts:458, wake-loop-cron.ts:343). Repo-wide search confirms SOVEREIGN_LEDGER_FAIL_CLOSED is NOT set in .env.example, .env.production.example, .env.docker.example, docker-compose, Dockerfiles, or CI — it appears only in code. Side-effect ordering confirmed at executor.ts:759-796: the tool side-effect has already executed and the step is marked `done` BEFORE safeSovereignLedger runs, so a fail-open ledger failure leaves a false-green with a missing regulator-mandated audit row and no downstream ok:false signal (the roll-back at 797-826 only fires when ledgerResult.ok===false, i.e. fail-closed only). The executor docstring (executor.ts:38-40) states 'Regulators demand fail-closed ... the hash-chained audit row is non-negotiable', contradicting the prod default. NUANCE vs the report: it is not fully 'silent' — the failure is logged via logger.error (executor.ts:968-973) — and the docstring frames fail-open as deliberate 'back-compat with W-Agency' (executor.ts:28-30), so this is a deliberate-but-wrong default rather than an accidental one; the gap is the absent downstream failure signal + missing audit row, which is real. Not in KNOWN_ISSUES.md nor audit-reports.
issueClass: half-state write / false-green over a missing regulator-mandated audit row
fileLine: packages/central-intelligence/src/kernel/agency/executor/executor.ts:949,974 (default fail-open) and 759-796 (side-effect-before-ledger ordering); env reader services/api-gateway/src/composition/service-registry.ts:3083-3096 (defaults false); composed at services/api-gateway/src/composition/sovereign.ts:380,458 and wake-loop-cron.ts:343
userImpact: On a sovereign-tier tool (eviction filing, owner payout, KRA MRI, GePG control-number revocation, market-rate override, inspection major-damage flag) whose external side-effect already executed, if the immutable hash-chained sovereign audit append throws (DB down, chain contention, network), the step still reports success and downstream callers receive NO sovereign-audit-write-failed signal to trigger reconciliation. The regulator-required row that reconstructs the action is silently absent. The invariant is opt-in via an env var that is unset everywhere.
proposedFix: Invert the default for sovereign-tier tools: readSovereignLedgerFailClosedFromEnv should default true (or executor should treat undefined as fail-closed when isSovereignTier(tool)), with an explicit env opt-OUT for legacy back-compat. Document SOVEREIGN_LEDGER_FAIL_CLOSED in the deploy env template and set it true in prod.

title: Gateway pino-http request logger has NO redact config — authorization bearer tokens, cookies, and client IP logged in plaintext on every request
reason: Independently confirmed. index.ts:596-598 builds the base logger as pino({ level: ... }) with no redact. index.ts:689 mounts pinoHttp({ logger }) with no redact and no custom serializers. Installed pino-http is v11.0.0; its logger.js wraps serializers.req (pino-std-serializers) as the default req serializer, and that serializer sets _req.headers = req.headers (req.js:88) and _req.remoteAddress (req.js:89). pino-http applies NO default redaction unless the caller passes `redact`. The gateway passes neither. So every HTTP access log line emits the full request headers — including Authorization (bearer token) and Cookie — plus the client IP, unredacted. The product is phone-OTP/bearer-keyed, and CLAUDE.md hard rule states Pino 'handles redaction'. Confirmed NOT in Docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md. The 12 additional bare pino({...}) route/middleware loggers (database.ts:59, public-marketing.hono.ts:45, missions/doc-chat/brain-* etc.) also lack redact, though I found no direct PII-field log calls in them today — the pino-http header/IP leak is the concretely reachable runtime exposure.
fileLine: services/api-gateway/src/index.ts:596-598 (base logger) and :689 (app.use(pinoHttp({ logger }))) — default req serializer logs req.headers (authorization, cookie) + remoteAddress with no redact
userImpact: Every request access-log line written by pino-http carries the caller's Authorization bearer token, cookies, and client IP in plaintext to stdout/log aggregators. A compromised or over-shared log store hands out live auth tokens and the platform's primary identity signals. GDPR Art. 30 / SOC2 exposure.
proposedFix: Pass a redact config to pino-http: pinoHttp({ logger, redact: { paths: ['req.headers.authorization','req.headers.cookie','req.remoteAddress','res.headers["set-cookie"]'], censor: '[REDACTED]' } }), or supply a custom req serializer that strips sensitive headers. Centralize one redacted pino factory (reuse @bossnyumba/observability DEFAULT_REDACT_FIELDS) and forbid bare pino( via lint for the remaining route loggers.

title: `test:e2e:local` npm script invokes a deleted Playwright project (`--project=customer-app`) → command always errors out
reason: Independently confirmed. package.json:11 ends with `playwright test --config=e2e/playwright.config.ts --project=customer-app`. e2e/playwright.config.ts:83-115 defines ONLY projects `setup`, `owner-portal`, `owner-live-journeys`; there is no `customer-app` project. docker-compose.e2e.yml defines services `admin-platform-portal` (port 3001:3000) and `owner-portal` (3000:80) — no customer-app service. title: Marketing chat shows EMPTY assistant bubbles when gateway streaming path is active (SSE event-name + field contract drift)
reason: Independently confirmed in code. The marketing widget IS LitFinChatPanel (apps/marketing/src/components/BossNyumbaWidgetMount.tsx mounts LitFinWidget with endpoint="/api/chat"; LitFinWidget.tsx:215 renders LitFinChatPanel; handleSend at LitFinChatPanel.tsx:212-222 routes SSE through readEventStream). readEventStream:699 skips every frame where currentEvent!=='message_chunk', and the gateway (public-marketing.hono.ts:260) emits event:<evt.type> where evt.type is turn_start/delta/handoff/turn_end (line 301: {type:'delta',content:...}). So delta frames are dropped. Secondary defect also confirmed: line 702 reads parsed.text ?? parsed.delta, never parsed.content. The Next route pipes gatewayRes.body verbatim (route.ts:325) with no event-name normalization, and no test guards readEventStream. CAVEAT downgrading from blocker: only reachable when NEXT_PUBLIC_API_GATEWAY_URL is set AND the gateway is reachable. apps/marketing/.vercel/.env.production.local sets it to "" (empty), so shipped Vercel production uses the direct-Anthropic JSON fallback (route.ts:354-366), which returns application/json and never enters readEventStream's streaming branch. The empty-bubble only manifests in local dev (.env.local=http://localhost:4011) or any self-hosted deployment that wires the gateway. Real contract drift, not a production blocker.
issueClass: FE/BE contract drift — broken stream / silent no-op
userImpact: On any deployment where the api-gateway is wired (NEXT_PUBLIC_API_GATEWAY_URL set + reachable), a visitor's marketing-chat question is answered by the server but the assistant bubble renders completely empty — the streaming indicator runs and nothing appears. Not reachable on the current Vercel production config (gateway URL empty → direct-Anthropic JSON path), so today's live marketing site is unaffected, but the bug fires the moment the intended gateway-first path is enabled.
proposedFix: Make readEventStream honor the gateway StreamTurnEvent contract: accept event names {delta, turn_start, handoff, turn_end, error} and read parsed.content (in addition to text/delta) for delta frames; surface SSE error frames into the bubble. Alternatively normalize event names to message_chunk/content inside the marketing /api/chat route when proxying the gateway body. Add a contract test that pipes a real public-marketing.hono.ts frame through readEventStream and asserts non-empty output.

title: Stored XSS: MarkdownCard citation sourceUri rendered into href with no scheme guard (javascript: passes schema)
reason: Independently confirmed. MarkdownCard.tsx:226-231 binds href={c.sourceUri} raw to a React anchor with NO safeHref guard and NO scheme check — unlike the inline-link path (renderInline line 77) which DOES gate on /^(https?:\/\/|\/|#)/. MarkdownCitationSchema.sourceUri (schemas/index.ts:367) is z.string().max(2000).optional() with no .refine, so safeParse (component line 142) succeeds on sourceUri='javascript:...'. The AdaptiveRenderer defense-in-depth re-validation (PART_SCHEMAS['markdown-card'] = MarkdownCardPartSchema, line 936) uses the SAME unrefined schema, so it does not block it either. Component is wired into GENUI_REGISTRY (registry.ts:73) and dispatched by AdaptiveRenderer, which is used in the shipped JarvisConsole surface (apps/admin-platform-portal/.../JarvisConsole.tsx renders TOOL_RESULT.uiPart). React 18.3.1 (confirmed installed) does NOT block javascript: hrefs at runtime — dev-only warning. No global DOMPurify/sanitize in the renderer path. The existing xss test (__tests__/markdown-card.xss.test.tsx:107) only rejects javascript: on the inline-link path, not the citation-list path. Not in KNOWN_ISSUES.md or any Docs audit. Reachable.
userImpact: A poisoned/jailbroken brain generation or injected-corpus citation can emit a markdown-card whose citations[].sourceUri = 'javascript:...'. The citation renders as a clickable anchor whose href executes arbitrary script on click in the owner/manager/tenant session — session-token/tenant-data theft or CSRF-style state change. CI is green because the regression test only covers the inline-link path.
proposedFix: Add `.refine((u)=>/^(https?:\/\/|\/)/.test(u),'sourceUri must be http(s) or path-relative')` to MarkdownCitationSchema.sourceUri (schemas/index.ts:367), and/or wrap the citation href at MarkdownCard.tsx:228 with a safeHref() helper mirroring EvidenceCard.tsx:24-28. Add a regression test for citations[].sourceUri='javascript:' asserting no live anchor / no javascript: href.

userImpact: On every backend-down/empty/offline banner across ~36 staff-mobile screens, an English-locale user sees Swahili text ('BossNyumba haijaunganishwa na seva...', 'Hakuna data bado...', 'Uko nje ya mtandao...') above the English line, and a Swahili-locale user sees the English line — a direct, high-blast-radius breach of the 'zero Swahili when en selected, and vice versa' rule.

title: Platform fee is computed and stored on the intent but never booked to the ledger on payment success
reason: Confirmed. createPayment computes platformFee/netAmount (orchestration:220-222) and stores them on the PaymentIntent (orchestration:236-237). bookPaymentToLedger posts only a 2-line journal — DEBIT holding gross / CREDIT customer-liability gross (orchestration:527-550) — with no PLATFORM_FEE leg, even though JournalTemplates already has a fee-split variant emitting PLATFORM_FEE legs (domain-models/src/ledger/ledger-entry.ts:194-251). DisbursementService.calculateDisbursementBreakdown sums entries of type 'PLATFORM_FEE' (disbursement.service.ts:717) that the payment path never creates. The owner-disbursement journal (JournalTemplates.ownerDisbursement, disbursement.service.ts:242) also has no fee leg. Real ledger-correctness gap regardless of breakdown-reader reachability. Not in KNOWN_ISSUES.
userImpact: Platform fee revenue is never recorded in the immutable ledger, and owner disbursement breakdowns report zero platform fees regardless of the fee charged — the ledger and the stated fee model disagree.
proposedFix: Book the fee split on payment success using the fee-aware JournalTemplates variant (DR holding gross, CR customer-liability net + CR platform-revenue fee, or equivalent balanced legs) so the ledger reflects the fee that was charged and the breakdown reader has real PLATFORM_FEE entries to sum.

title: Second platform-fee formula in DisbursementService diverges from the canonical engine (round vs floor, percent vs bps)
reason: Confirmed at code level. DisbursementService.calculatePlatformFee (disbursement.service.ts:776-779) computes Math.round(grossAmount.amountMinorUnits * feePercent / 100) — a round-based percent formula. The canonical engine is lib/platform-fee.ts calculatePlatformFeeMinor = Math.floor((amountMinor * bps) / 10_000), and domain-extensions.ts:60-82 documents that A-BUG #14 consolidated everything to that one floor-based formula (the domain-extensions calculatePlatformFee now REDIRECTS to it). This DisbursementService copy is a genuine second formula that can differ by one minor unit. Confirmed born-dark: grep finds zero non-test, non-dist callers of calculatePlatformFee/calculateNetAmount/previewDisbursement/calculateDisbursementBreakdown outside disbursement.service.ts (previewDisbursement→calculateDisbursementBreakdown→calculatePlatformFee are internally chained but have no external caller). Severity is appropriately medium given born-dark status. Not in KNOWN_ISSUES.
userImpact: If/when the disbursement preview is wired, the fee shown to owners can differ by a minor unit from the fee the ledger/statement engine books — re-introducing exactly the two-formula drift the #14 consolidation eliminated.
proposedFix: Delete DisbursementService.calculatePlatformFee and route calculateNetAmount/previewDisbursement through the canonical calculatePlatformFeeMinor(amountMinor, bps) so there is exactly one fee formula in the service.

title: Money.toString() and amountMajorUnits hard-code /100, wrong for 0-decimal currencies (TZS/UGX/RWF/JPY)
reason: Confirmed at code level. The Money prototype augmentation defines toString() as `${this.currency} ${(this.amountMinorUnits / 100).toFixed(2)}` (domain-extensions.ts:127-129) and amountMajorUnits getter as this.amountMinorUnits / 100 (domain-extensions.ts:131-139) — both hard-code a 2-decimal divisor and ignore decimalsForCurrency(), which DOES exist (packages/domain-models/src/common/money.ts). For 0-decimal TZS/UGX, TZS 5000 renders 'TZS 50.00' and amountMajorUnits returns 50. amountMajorUnits feeds the M-Pesa STK and B2C Amount fields via Math.round(params.amount.amountMajorUnits) at mpesa-provider.ts:248 and :402. Currently masked because mpesaProvider is registered KES-only (server.ts:457 currencies:['KES']) and KES is 2-decimal — but this directly contradicts the CLAUDE.md hard rule (multi-currency, TZ at launch, never hard-code currency precision). Not in KNOWN_ISSUES.
userImpact: Any TZS/UGX amount logged via toString() or routed through amountMajorUnits is off by 100x. The moment M-Pesa (or any amountMajorUnits consumer) is enabled for a 0-decimal currency, an STK push for TZS 5000 would request 50 from the customer — a 100x undercharge.
proposedFix: Make toString() and amountMajorUnits currency-aware via decimalsForCurrency()/minorUnitDivisor() from money.ts (or use toDecimal/formatMoney), and have the M-Pesa provider perform an explicit currency-aware conversion rather than the hard-coded /100 getter.

title: `onboarding_sessions` / `onboarding_session_events` are RLS-ENABLED with tenant policies but never FORCE'd — table-owner role bypasses tenant isolation
reason: Independently confirmed at 0164:111-136: both tables carry tenant_id, get ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY + onb_sessions_tenant_isolation / onb_events_tenant_isolation policies, but NO FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY. Verified across all 321 migrations: grep for `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` matching 'onboarding' returns only the DIFFERENT table onboarding_state (0278:60); these two tables appear in zero FORCE roster — not 0173 (post-0156 sweep lists only tool_call_denylist + pre-0156 legacy tables), not 0179b/0311/0314/0316/0317. This violates the CLAUDE.md hard rule 'RLS is FORCE-enabled on every tenant-scoped table.' Not in Docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md. Without FORCE, the table-owner/migration-runner role bypasses the tenant_isolation policy. NUANCE that lowers severity from the claimed 'high': no current runtime code writes these tables — the only SessionStore implementation is InMemorySessionStore (session-store.ts:153); the 'drizzle-backed SessionStore' referenced in readyz.ts:10 / index.ts:39 comments does not exist as an implemented class (grep `implements SessionStore` yields only InMemorySessionStore), and the api-gateway onboarding.hono.ts route uses in-memory Maps (sessions = new Map). So the data-exposure is latent (no production rows on any wired path today) while the shipped schema invariant violation is real.
userImpact: DB-level: any owner-roled connection (migration runner, leaked service_role, owner psql/worker that forgot to drop privileges) bypasses tenant_isolation and can read/write any tenant's onboarding sessions once the db-backed store is wired. Today the tables are unwritten (in-memory store only), so impact is latent, but the FORCE-RLS hard-rule violation ships in the migration and will bite when staging/prod db mode lands.
proposedFix: Append a forward migration: `ALTER TABLE public.onboarding_sessions FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;` and `ALTER TABLE public.onboarding_session_events FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;` (table-existence-guarded, idempotent), plus `REVOKE ALL ON public.onboarding_sessions FROM anon;` and on the events table to match the canonical 0311/0316 contract. Add both names to the FORCE-coverage assertion once it exists (see finding #3).

title: FORCE-RLS CI invariant test claimed by migration 0173 does not exist — missing-FORCE regressions are not caught in CI
reason: Independently confirmed. (1) 0173:225-228 explicitly claims 'The companion test at packages/database/src/__tests__/force-rls-coverage.test.ts parses every migration and asserts the invariant statically, so a future migration that adds RLS without FORCE will fail CI.' (2) That file does not exist — `find ... -name force-rls-coverage*` returns nothing across the whole tree. (3) Both live scanners lack FORCE detection: grep `force` against scripts/audit-rls-coverage.mjs returns ZERO matches, and scripts/audit/check-rls-coverage.mjs only references FORCE in usage/comment lines, with its actual logic keying on `ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` (line 130/137/203) + tenant policy. (4) Proof of the consequence: audit-reports/rls-coverage.json:1202-1209 records onboarding_sessions as `hasRlsEnabled: true, hasTenantPolicy: true, coveredByFile: 0164` — i.e. the scanner declared it fully covered while never checking FORCE, which is exactly how finding #2's gap shipped unguarded. The two real RLS tests (rls-guc-bind.test.ts, rls-isolation.integration.test.ts) test GUC binding and single-table enforcement, not a cross-migration FORCE invariant. Not in KNOWN_ISSUES.
userImpact: The stated CI safety net that would have caught finding #2 is fictional. Every RLS-enabling migration since 0173 that omits FORCE ships unguarded and silently regresses the FORCE-RLS hard rule; the platform believes an invariant is locked in CI that is in fact unenforced.
proposedFix: Either (a) create packages/database/src/__tests__/force-rls-coverage.test.ts that static-parses every migration and asserts each table receiving ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY also receives FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY (whitespace-tolerant: the repo mixes `FORCE ROW` and `FORCE  ROW` with two spaces — see 0317:55/104), OR (b) add a FORCE_RLS_RE + hasRlsForced column to scripts/audit-rls-coverage.mjs gated under enforce mode. Then correct/remove the false claim in 0173:225-228.

reason: Independently confirmed. PersonaDriftClient.tsx:42 returns `${trimmed}/api/v1/persona-drift/events`; fetched on mount at line 58 and on setInterval(fetchEvents, POLL_INTERVAL_MS=60_000) at line 78. page.tsx present in app/persona-drift/ (reachable via file-based routing even if not in StaffNav). title: Outbox at-least-once path is born-dark: no durable IOutboxStore implementation exists and the outbound webhooks-service has zero callers / no idempotency-key header
reason: Confirmed. getEventBus in packages/observability/src/event-bus.ts takes config (no merge of a passed outboxStore at call time) and the EventBus constructor defaults outboxStore to new MemoryOutboxStore() (line 171). outbox-processor/src/index.ts:221-224 calls getEventBus({serviceName,enableOutbox:true}) WITHOUT outboxStore, so despite the DA3 OUTBOX_STORE_TYPE=redis|postgres guard (which only validates the env var), the resolved store is still MemoryOutboxStore. grep confirms MemoryOutboxStore is the ONLY class implementing IOutboxStore in the entire repo — no Postgres/Redis impl. Outbound webhooks-service: src/index.ts only re-exports (no HTTP server); grep finds zero importers of @bossnyumba/webhooks-service / webhook-service.trigger outside the package itself; subscriptions are a process-local Map (webhook-service.ts:12); deliver() (delivery.ts:186-192) sends X-Webhook-Timestamp + X-Webhook-Signature but no X-Webhook-Id/Idempotency-Key; trigger() retry loop (webhook-service.ts:57-71) wraps deliver()'s own retry loop (delivery.ts:198-206) = double retry. CLAUDE.md hard rule 'webhook delivery is at-least-once; consumers MUST be idempotent via Idempotency-Key' is unmet on the outbound side.
userImpact: There is no reachable durable outbound webhook delivery. If activated it would emit duplicate POSTs (service retry x delivery retry) with no idempotency key for consumers to dedupe on, with subscriptions stored per-process (invisible across replicas / lost on restart). The standalone outbox-processor, if replicas flip from 0, drains a private in-memory store the gateway never writes to.
proposedFix: Implement a Postgres- or Redis-backed IOutboxStore and wire it via getEventBus({ outboxStore }) in BOTH api-gateway and outbox-processor; have the DA3 guard fail when the resolved store is still MemoryOutboxStore. For the outbound webhooks-service: add a stable X-Webhook-Id (event id) header in deliver(), remove the double retry loop in webhook-service.trigger() (delegate retries to deliver()), back subscriptions with a shared store, and either wire the service into the system or delete it as dead code.

title: reconcileWithProvider loops an unbounded set of PROCESSING payments making one external provider API call per row
reason: Confirmed: findNeedingReconciliation (drizzle-payment-intent.repository.ts:404-420) selects every PROCESSING payment older than cutoff with NO .limit(). reconcileWithProvider (reconciliation.service.ts:331-382) loops paymentsToCheck and calls provider.getPaymentIntentStatus(externalId) once per row (line 349), serially. Reachable in shipped runtime via POST /api/v1/admin/jobs/reconciliation (server.ts:1875 → runProviderReconciliation → reconcileWithProvider) and POST /api/v1/reconciliation/run (server.ts:2192). Under a provider outage/webhook backlog a single tick loads all stuck PROCESSING rows and fires a serial storm of provider calls with no per-tick ceiling and no overlap guard. Not in KNOWN_ISSUES/audit.
issueClass: unbounded list read + N+1 external calls in a loop (no batch ceiling)
userImpact: When a backlog of PROCESSING payments accumulates, one cron tick loads them all and issues a serial flood of provider API calls — slow, prone to provider rate-limiting/timeouts, and can run past the next tick causing overlapping runs that hammer the provider further, degrading the very recovery path meant to unstick payments.
proposedFix: Add a bounded limit (process at most N oldest-first per tick) to findNeedingReconciliation and the loop, use bounded concurrency for provider calls, carry remaining work to the next tick, and add an overlap guard.

title: 5 tenant-scoped MCP template resources (tenant/property/unit/case/graph-entity) are born-dark on the mounted gateway transport — resources/read only calls readStaticResource
reason: Confirmed in services/api-gateway/src/routes/mcp.hono.ts: resources/read (224-232) only calls mcp.readStaticResource(uri); resources/list (214-222) advertises only mcp.staticResources; there is no resources/templates/list method. In packages/mcp-server, readTemplateResource / resolveTemplateResource (bossnyumba-mcp-server.ts:228-234, mcp-resources.ts:206-262) have ZERO production callers (grep: only the definition, the index.ts re-export, and the SDK-native registration at line 361-380 which iterates staticResources ONLY). A template URI (bossnyumba://tenant/<id> etc.) therefore reaches resolveStaticResource's default branch (mcp-resources.ts:201-202 'Unknown static resource'), which is caught at mcp.hono.ts:277-283 and surfaced as JSON-RPC -32603. The guardVariable path-traversal guard and tenant-scoping in resolveTemplateResource are dead code on this transport. CAVEAT the hunter overstated discoverability: clients cannot enumerate these templates from the mounted transport (resources/list omits them), so reaching this requires an out-of-band/known URI. Also the underlying resolvers (mcp-wiring.ts:469-483 tenantProfile/propertyDetail/etc.) are stubs that echo {id,tenantId} — so even if wired the payloads would be near-empty.
fileLine: services/api-gateway/src/routes/mcp.hono.ts:214-232 (resources/list + resources/read, static-only); packages/mcp-server/src/bossnyumba-mcp-server.ts:228-234 + mcp-resources.ts:206-262 (template path, zero callers)
userImpact: Any per-entity resource read over the only mounted MCP transport (/api/v1/mcp) for a template URI fails with an opaque -32603 internal error rather than a tenant-scoped payload. The entire advertised template-resource surface is unreachable; agents cannot fetch a single tenant/property/unit/case/graph-entity via this transport.
proposedFix: In mcp.hono.ts resources/read, match the URI against BOSSNYUMBA_RESOURCE_TEMPLATES.uriTemplate, extract the path variable, and call mcp.readTemplateResource(uri, variables, context). Add a resources/templates/list method returning the templates so clients can discover them. Implement real tenant-scoped resolvers (not the current echo stubs) and add a regression test asserting resources/read of bossnyumba://tenant/<id> returns the scoped payload, not -32603.

title: observability Logger redaction covers only 3 nesting depths (field, *.field, *.*.field) — phone/token nested 4+ deep escapes redaction
reason: Confirmed with a citation correction. logger.ts:102-106 builds pino redact.paths as exactly three literal levels (f, *.${f}, *.*.${f}); pino redact does not recurse arbitrarily, so a field at depth 4+ is not censored. The package DOES ship a recursive walker — redactPII (packages/observability/src/pii-redactor.ts:128, DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH=12 at :78) and wrapLoggerWithRedaction (:208) — and logger.ts never imports or calls either (confirmed: no pii-redactor/redactPII import in logger.ts). NOTE: the finding cited the walker as 'logging/pii-redactor.ts'; it actually lives at packages/observability/src/pii-redactor.ts (the logging/ dir holds only logger.ts + logger.test.ts). The Logger is used in shipped code (packages/truth-engine/src/logger.ts:13 wraps createLogger; tenant-mobile also imports it), so the depth-limited redaction is in a shipped path. Severity medium is right: it requires PII specifically nested ≥4 levels in a log payload to actually leak, which I could not prove flows today — the config gap is real but its exploitability is conditional.

title: Open redirect after login via unvalidated `next` query param
reason: Independently confirmed. LoginForm.tsx:15 `const next = params.get('next') ?? '/'` reads next directly from the URL query with no same-origin/leading-slash validation; on res.ok the code does `window.location.href = next` (line 30). The middleware only ever sets next to a relative path via encodeURIComponent(pathname+search) (middleware.ts), but LoginForm trusts the raw query, so /login?next=https://evil.example/phish flows straight to window.location.href. Reachability: the login route (api/platform/login/route.ts) is a LIVE proxy to identity-service /sessions (not a hardcoded 503 stub), so a successful login is a real shipped path — on success the redirect fires to the attacker URL. Note line is :15 not :16 as cited (off by one); :30 is exact. Not in KNOWN_ISSUES.
userImpact: An attacker sends an HQ staff member /login?next=https://evil.example/phish. After a legitimate successful login, the staffer is redirected to an attacker-controlled external site — a post-auth redirect / credential-phishing vector against platform staff.
proposedFix: Validate next before redirecting: accept only same-origin relative paths (must start with a single '/', reject '//', reject any scheme/host, e.g. via `new URL(next, location.origin)` origin check), else fall back to '/'.

title: Tenant cold-start login race — fixed 280ms splash timer reads isAuthenticated() once and can bounce a signed-in user to /auth/login
reason: Confirmed. apps/tenant-mobile/app/index.tsx:11-23 sets ready=true after a hardcoded 280ms setTimeout, then calls isAuthenticated() exactly once and Redirects. isAuthenticated() (session.ts:105) returns Boolean(currentUser?.id); currentUser is populated only by the async ensureBootstrapped() (session.ts:65-99), which awaits supabase.auth.getSession() (SecureStore read + possible token-refresh network call). index.tsx never calls useSession()/subscribe(), so it neither triggers bootstrap itself nor re-renders when it completes; bootstrap is kicked off in parallel by EventStreamMount→useSession (_layout.tsx:26) but there is no happens-before guarantee against the 280ms timer. If getSession() resolves after 280ms (common on cold start / slow network) the redirect to /auth/login already fired. Medium: intermittent and recoverable. Not in KNOWN_ISSUES.
userImpact: A logged-in tenant is intermittently dumped on the login screen on cold launch despite a valid persisted session — a flaky, confidence-eroding login→home experience.
proposedFix: Gate the splash on real session state: have index.tsx call useSession() with an explicit `ready` flag set true only after ensureBootstrapped resolves, and redirect off that — not a fixed timer.

title: AI audit-chain verifier is canonical-form-incompatible with live ai_audit_chain writers; tamper cron false-fires for every tenant
reason: The HASH-SCHEME INCOMPATIBILITY is independently confirmed and real: the live writers (services/api-gateway/src/composition/brain-tools/outcome-predictor.ts:162-164 and services/api-gateway/src/workers/outcome-reconciliation-worker.ts:479-481, the latter started at index.ts:2390) write rows to ai_audit_chain using plain createHash('sha256').update(lastHash + canonical) with genesis prev_hash='' and a canonical that omits sequenceId/turnId/timestamp; the ai-copilot verifier (packages/ai-copilot/src/security/audit-hash-chain.ts:111 GENESIS_PREV_HASH='GENESIS_0000...', :161-194 canonicalRow/hashAuditPayload over {sequenceId,prevHash,tenantId,turnId,action,payload,timestamp} under HMAC) would return 'prevHash mismatch at 1' on the first row. HOWEVER the finding's stated runtime IMPACT is not reachable: the auditVerifyCron supervisor (service-registry.ts:2988-3007) is constructed but is NEVER referenced or .start()-ed anywhere in services/api-gateway/src/index.ts (grep for auditVerifyCron in index.ts returns nothing; the only .start() is in its own unit test audit-verify-cron.test.ts with injected mock verifier/tenants), and suite.auditChain.verifyChain/verifyRandomSample have no HTTP route consumer (sovereign-ledger.hono.ts:175 calls a DIFFERENT ledger service). So no verify cycle ever runs in the shipped runtime: there are no 'AI AUDIT CHAIN TAMPER DETECTED' logs and no ai-audit.tampered bus events 'every cycle for every tenant'. The control is a born-dark / non-functional security organ (broken if ever wired), not a production blocker false-firing today. Severity 'blocker' and the 'permanent false alarm' impact are not substantiated; the verifier-writer drift itself is a genuine latent defect.
issueClass: born-dark security organ / writer-verifier contract drift (verifier unwired)
fileLine: packages/ai-copilot/src/security/audit-hash-chain.ts:111,161-194,420-436; verifier wired-but-never-started at services/api-gateway/src/composition/service-registry.ts:2988-3007 (no .start() in index.ts); incompatible live writers at services/api-gateway/src/composition/brain-tools/outcome-predictor.ts:135-187 and services/api-gateway/src/workers/outcome-reconciliation-worker.ts:455-499
userImpact: Today: none observable — the verifier never executes (cron unstarted, no HTTP surface), so no false TAMPER alarms are emitted. The deeper exposure is latent: the tamper-evident AI audit control is non-functional end-to-end (incompatible schemes), so if the cron is ever started or an admin verify route is added it would either flag every tenant or be unable to validate genuine forgeries. The 'hash-chained, append-only' rule is effectively unenforced at the verify layer, but no operator-facing false alarm exists in the shipped path.
proposedFix: Before wiring the verifier, unify ONE canonical-hash + genesis primitive across writers and verifier: either route all ai_audit_chain appends through AuditHashChain.append() (HMAC + GENESIS_PREV_HASH), or change the verifier's canonicalRow/genesis to match the deployed writers' scheme (SHA-256(lastHash+canonical), prev_hash '' genesis, identical field set). Add a cross-package contract test asserting a row written by the production writer verifies clean. Separately decide whether the auditVerifyCron should be started at all (it currently is dead in index.ts).

title: persona-runtime scope gate diverges between evaluate (deny) and renderScopeFilter (tenant-wide) on missing org/module/region id
reason: The divergence is independently confirmed: evaluateScopePredicate (packages/persona-runtime/src/scope-predicate.ts:99-156) returns allowed:false for org_scope/module_scope/region_scope when both predicate id and ctx id are undefined, while renderScopeFilter (:217-234) falls back to {block:false, tenantId} (whole-tenant) on the same missing id — opposite fail directions. Born-dark is also confirmed: grep across services/, apps/, and all other packages/ shows NO caller of renderScopeFilter or evaluateScopePredicate outside the persona-runtime package barrel (src/index.ts re-export), the dist .d.ts files, and the package's own __tests__. capability-tools.ts and brain-voice.hono.ts import only capability-disclosure helpers / BUILT_IN_PERSONAS, not the scope gate. So this is a genuine fail-open divergence in an exported-but-unwired function — a real latent footgun, correctly characterized by the hunter as born-dark (no live breach today).
fileLine: packages/persona-runtime/src/scope-predicate.ts:99-156 (evaluate denies on missing id) vs :217-234 (renderScopeFilter returns tenant-wide on same missing id)
userImpact: No live impact today — renderScopeFilter has no caller in services/ or apps/. If a repository ever wires renderScopeFilter for a persona whose scoping id is unresolved, it would emit a tenant-wide WHERE clause instead of an empty result, an org/module/region containment breach. Primed footgun, not an active leak.
proposedFix: Make renderScopeFilter fail-closed to {block:true} whenever the scoping id resolves to undefined for org/module/region, matching evaluateScopePredicate's deny semantics, and extract a shared helper so the two paths cannot drift. Either wire the gate into a real repository or delete the unused exports.

title: Marketing chat ignores EN/SW UI toggle entirely on the gateway path — locale-mixing / wrong-language replies
reason: Confirmed in code. tryGateway (route.ts:224-246) forwards only {sessionId, message} (line 238) — never language. ChatTurnSchema (public-marketing.hono.ts:51-64) has no language field. buildMarketingSystemPrompt (marketing-persona.ts:147-152) accepts only visitorCountry/visitorRole/sessionSeed/fewShotCount — no language param and no single-language lock; the persona body actively contains 'Match language to their world' (line 118) and 'Talk to your phone in Swahili' (line 110). The direct-Anthropic fallback (route.ts:251 + SYSTEM_PROMPT_EN/SW) DOES lock language hard, so the two paths diverge. CAVEAT: like Finding 1, the gateway path is only active when the gateway is wired; on the current Vercel prod (gateway URL empty) the locale-locked direct-Anthropic path is the live path, so production today is NOT mixing. Downgraded from high to medium for that reason — real code/architecture drift that bites any gateway-enabled deployment.
issueClass: Locale purity — single-language-per-locale broken on the gateway path
userImpact: On any gateway-enabled deployment the EN/SW widget toggle is a dead control for the marketing chat: Mr. Mwikila replies in whatever language the model infers, so an English-locked visitor who types one Swahili word can get a Swahili reply (and vice-versa) — the exact mixing CLAUDE.md forbids. Not reachable on the current Vercel prod config (direct-Anthropic path locks language), so the live marketing site is unaffected until the gateway path is enabled.
proposedFix: Forward language from the widget through tryGateway into the gateway body; add language: z.enum(['en','sw']).optional() to ChatTurnSchema; thread it into buildMarketingSystemPrompt and prepend the same hard EN-only/SW-only locale lock the Next route already uses for the direct path.

title: Owner-portal floating widget tab strip shows English titles for Swahili owners — locale never threaded into useChatTabBridge
reason: Confirmed in code. MwikilaWidgetMount.tsx:27 calls useChatTabBridge() with no options, so locale defaults to 'en' (useChatTabBridge.ts:60). LocaleProvider/useLocaleContext exists (apps/owner-portal/src/contexts/LocaleProvider.tsx) and is not consulted here. pickPayloadTitle (tab-sse-parser.ts:216-227) correctly returns titleSw for locale 'sw' but is only ever called with 'en'. The gateway bridge does carry titleSw into the tab_spawn payload (chat-tab-bridge.ts:155), so the SW title plumbing is real shelfware. Reachability depends on the brain emitting a titleSw= attribute on the inline tab tag (designed contract via staff-tools.ts tab tools), which is the intended behaviour; even when titleSw is present it is ignored because locale is never passed. Real wiring drift.
issueClass: Locale purity / dead wiring — locale param unused
userImpact: A Swahili-preference owner gets chat-spawned tab titles in English while the rest of the owner-portal UI is Swahili — language mixing on the same surface. Impact is bounded by whether the brain actually emits titleSw on the tag (when it omits it, the code already falls back to the single default title), so the worst case is bilingual-tag turns rendering the EN variant.
proposedFix: Read the active owner locale from LocaleProvider (useLocaleContext) in MwikilaWidgetMount and pass useChatTabBridge({ locale }). Add a test asserting a sw owner gets titleSw when the payload carries it.

title: Conversation-feel anti-call-center guards are no-ops on the user-visible path (streaming AND JSON)
reason: Confirmed in code, with a correction to the finding's framing. On the SSE path (ai-chat.hono.ts:288-356) pipeStreamTurnToSSE streams the raw orchestrator deltas to the user at line 328 BEFORE auditChatResponse runs at line 331, and the audit only emits an observability 'auditor' event (lines 342-350) — cleanedText is never sent. auditChatResponse (chat-response-gate.ts:291-292,361) computes cleanedText via cleanChatResponse but returns it unused. CORRECTION TO FINDING: the finding asserts the filler-stripping DOES apply on the non-stream JSON path; it does not. brain.hono.ts (the JSON brain-turn endpoint, lines 426-452 and 466-480) feeds enforceEvidenceRule the RAW turn.responseText, and enforceEvidenceRule (lines 290-311) returns either responseText (raw) or a rejection string — it never reads verdict.cleanedText. A repo-wide grep confirms NO caller ever consumes verdict.cleanedText. So the stripper is shelfware on every user-visible path, not just streaming — the underlying defect is real and broader than reported.
issueClass: Missing logic / shelfware on the hot path
userImpact: The 'human-like voice / anti-call-center' filler-stripping (stripChatbotFeel / stripTheatreFromUncertainty) never reaches the user on any chat surface — neither the SSE path that owner/manager widgets use nor the JSON brain-turn path. Scripted-feel phrases the guards were built to remove still appear in replies. The conversation-feel package is effectively dead despite being 'wired' into the audit.
proposedFix: On the JSON path, surface verdict.cleanedText in place of the raw responseText when not rejected. On the SSE path, run stripChatbotFeel as a streaming transform before pipeStreamTurnToSSE (or buffer+clean before flush). At minimum, stop advertising the guards as enforced on chat and document the streaming exception.

title: ManagerChat teaching surface hard-codes language="en" everywhere — Swahili scaffolding never rendered

title: LedgerService.voidEntry posts a single-line (unbalanced) journal that always throws — born-dark and broken
reason: Confirmed at code level. voidEntry (ledger.service.ts:834-880) builds a CreateJournalEntryRequest with a SINGLE CORRECTION line (lines 847-870) and calls postJournalEntry. validateJournalBalance (domain-models/src/ledger/ledger-entry.ts:114-139) sums debits/credits per currency and returns false unless they are equal; one line can never balance, so postJournalEntry throws 'Journal entry is not balanced' at ledger.service.ts:189 for any non-zero amount. reason: Confirmed at code level. POST /api/v1/accounts/:id/entries (server.ts:852-903) posts a SINGLE line (lines 875-885) through postJournalEntry, which validateJournalBalance (domain-models/src/ledger/ledger-entry.ts:114-139) always rejects for a non-zero single line — the route can never succeed. userImpact: Manual journal entries can be duplicated by a simple retry, mutating balances; and the single-account-entry route is dead (always 500s 'not balanced'). No production gateway caller exercises either, limiting blast radius today.
proposedFix: Accept and forward an Idempotency-Key on /api/v1/journal (thread it into postJournalEntry options). For /accounts/:id/entries, either require a balancing counter-leg or remove the route, since a lone entry violates double-entry.

title: assertApproved skips tenant-binding when the approval record's tenantId is null — a platform-scoped approval would authorize a tenant-scoped action (latent: no production caller)
reason: Independently confirmed as a latent defect, accurately self-scoped low. The tenant-binding guard at assertions.ts:412-417 requires record.tenantId to be truthy (line 415: `record.tenantId &&`), so when record.tenantId is null/undefined the mismatch check short-circuits and execution falls through to `return { ok: true, record }` (line 425) for ANY supplied args.tenantId — a platform-scoped approval satisfies a tenant-scoped consume. Separately, isApprovalExpired (assertions.ts:342) returns false (never-expires) when expires.getTime() is NaN, failing OPEN on a malformed expiresAt. CRITICAL gating fact confirmed: assertApproved has ZERO production callers — repo-wide grep shows references only in assertions.ts itself, barrel re-exports (index.ts:95, policy-gate/index.ts:45), the doc comment, and assertions.test.ts. The executor consumes approvals via approvalGate.markExecuted, not this helper. So this is a trap for the next caller, not a live break — exactly as the hunter scoped it (low / latent). Not in KNOWN_ISSUES.md nor audit-reports.
issueClass: IDOR-adjacent / missing scope cross-check (latent — no production caller yet)
userImpact: If a future caller wires assertApproved as its approval gate, a platform-scoped (null-tenant) four-eye approval could be consumed to authorize a side effect bound to an arbitrary tenant, defeating per-tenant approval isolation; and a malformed expiresAt would make the approval never expire. No live impact today (helper has no production caller).
proposedFix: Treat a null record.tenantId combined with a supplied args.tenantId as a mismatch (deny) unless the action is explicitly platform-scoped; make isApprovalExpired fail CLOSED (treat unparseable expiresAt as expired). Add a test asserting a platform approval cannot satisfy a tenant-scoped consume.

title: Standalone NIN/OPay/NGGIS MCP servers fail OPEN on tenant allowlist when NODE_ENV != 'production' and accept model-supplied tenantId
reason: Logic confirmed identical across services/mcp-server-{nin,opay,nggis}/src/index.ts: allowlistResolved = allowlist ?? (NODE_ENV==='production' ? [] : null) (nin 162-164, opay/nggis 127-129); the guard `if (allowlistResolved && ...)` is skipped when null; tenantId falls back to caller-supplied argsTenantId when no _meta.verifiedTenantId (nin 146-150); and main() wires StdioServerTransport (nin 211, opay/nggis 161) which never injects _meta.verifiedTenantId. So with NODE_ENV unset/dev/staging/CI and no MCP_TENANT_ALLOWLIST, any stdio caller can pass an arbitrary tenantId with no gate. This is a genuine fail-open. SEVERITY RECALIBRATED DOWN, not eliminated: (a) the DEFAULT adapter is a deterministic MOCK (MockNinAdapter/MockOpayAdapter/MockNggisAdapter at line 76/51) — the file headers state the real NIMC/OPay/NGGIS REST clients are a future phase; (b) all three packages are `private:true`, depended on by nothing, and injected/instantiated by NO composition root anywhere in this repo (grep for createNinServer/NimcNivsAdapter/etc. in services/api-gateway = zero hits); (c) the bypass is explicitly non-production-only. The cross-tenant real-PII/payment/land leak the hunter describes requires a real adapter that is never wired here, so it is not reachable on any shipped path today.
issueClass: fail-open guard / tenant clamp from model output
userImpact: If any of these standalone stdio servers is ever deployed with a real adapter and NODE_ENV unset/non-prod and no allowlist, one principal could query KYC/payment/land-registry under an arbitrary tenant id — a tenant-isolation bypass. Today the impact is latent: default mock adapter, not deployed, not wired; the risk is a future-phase footgun, not a live exposure.
proposedFix: Fail closed regardless of NODE_ENV: when allowlist is unset, default allowlistResolved to deny-all ([]) in every environment, and require _meta.verifiedTenantId for any real-adapter path (never treat args.tenantId as authoritative for scoping). title: renderMemoryNamespaceKey collapses a missing user_id to literal 'nil', merging own-records personas' private memory into one shared bucket
reason: Code confirmed at packages/persona-runtime/src/seeds.ts:342-349: every unset token, including user_id, is replaced with the literal 'nil' (:348 `args.tokens.user_id ?? 'nil'`). Two distinct principals with an absent user_id both render the same '...:user:nil' namespace key. Born-dark confirmed: grep shows no caller of renderMemoryNamespaceKey outside seeds.ts, the package barrel re-export, the dist .d.ts, and the package's own __tests__/seeds.test.ts. The behavior is real and the cross-user merge risk is real-if-wired; correctly flagged as latent/born-dark. Low severity is appropriate.
issueClass: born-dark organ / latent cross-user memory-key collision
userImpact: None today — the helper has no production caller. If wired as intended for an own-records / user-scoped persona invoked without a resolved user_id, two principals would read/write the same 'nil' memory namespace — a customer-to-customer memory leak. Latent only.
proposedFix: Throw (or return a per-request unique sentinel) when a required template token such as user_id is missing for own-records / user-scoped templates, instead of collapsing to the shared 'nil' literal; validate token presence against the template's declared dimensions before rendering.

title: Tool-catalog channel comment vs code mismatch: 'EMPTY channels = web only' but empty channels skip the channel check
reason: Confirmed: the comment at packages/persona-runtime/src/tool-catalog.ts:38 states 'EMPTY = web only' but the guard at :98 `if (desc?.channels && desc.channels.length > 0)` skips the tool-level channel check entirely for an empty channels array. However the practical exposure is bounded and the finding's own framing is accurate: (a) computeToolCatalog is born-dark — no caller exists in services/ or apps/ outside the package barrel and tests; and (b) even if wired, the persona-level channelAllowlist guard at :109 still constrains, so it is defence-in-depth, not a breach. issueClass: doc/code mismatch in a born-dark function (over-permissive comment, allowlist backstop intact)
fileLine: packages/persona-runtime/src/tool-catalog.ts:38 (comment 'EMPTY = web only') vs :98 (empty channels array skips the tool-level channel gate)
userImpact: No live impact — computeToolCatalog is not invoked in services/ or apps/. proposedFix: Pick one and make code match comment: either treat channels:[] as ['web'] to enforce the documented semantics, or fix the comment to read 'EMPTY = no tool-level channel restriction'.

title: Marketing AI-unavailable error renders raw code '(ai_unavailable)' to the visitor; SSE error frames render nothing
reason: Confirmed both halves. JSON path: the marketing route returns 503 NextResponse.json({error:'ai_unavailable', ...}) (route.ts:367-375). The widget always sends accept:text/event-stream, but a 503 comes back as application/json, so contentType.includes('text/event-stream') is false and the JSON branch runs: reply = json?.error ? `(${json.error})` (LitFinChatPanel.tsx:238-239) → literally renders '(ai_unavailable)' (untranslated, not the EN/SW friendly copy at 240-242 which is only used when error is absent). Stream path: a gateway event:error frame is skipped by readEventStream (line 699, currentEvent!=='message_chunk'), so on an outage mid-stream the bubble stays empty. Both reachable.
userImpact: On an AI outage the visitor sees the raw machine code '(ai_unavailable)' (untranslated) on the JSON path, or an empty bubble with no error at all on the stream path — a confusing dead-end with no recovery hint and no EN/SW friendly copy.
proposedFix: Map known error codes (ai_unavailable, rate_limited, etc.) to localized EN/SW copy in the JSON branch; make readEventStream surface SSE error frames into the bubble using the same localized fallback as the catch branch (lines 272-274).

title: Marketing/owner widget message bubble can hang in perpetual streaming state when stream ends without turn_end
reason: Confirmed in code. In useUnifiedChat.ts the per-message isStreaming flag and activeMwikilaIdRef are cleared ONLY inside onEvent on event.type==='turn_end'||'error' (lines 136-147). useChatStream clears its own state.isStreaming in a finally (useChatStream.ts:287) regardless. The only useEffect in useUnifiedChat (lines 93-95) just mirrors mode into modeRef — there is NO effect reconciling the message isStreaming flag from stream.state.isStreaming. So if the orchestrator stream closes cleanly without yielding turn_end (or that frame is lost), the bubble stays isStreaming:true and activeMwikilaIdRef stays set. Real, but a narrow edge case: the gateway streamTurn normally always emits turn_end, and an error event also clears it — so it only strands on an abnormal close that omits turn_end. Matches the finding's own low/medium rating.
fileLine: packages/chat-ui/src/widget/useUnifiedChat.ts:136-147 (no useEffect reconciling message isStreaming from stream.state)
userImpact: If a stream closes without a turn_end frame, the owner MAIN/FLOATING widget bubble keeps showing the typing indicator indefinitely after the reply is complete, and the lingering activeMwikilaIdRef can block the next send, requiring a reload. Edge-case only (normal turns emit turn_end).
proposedFix: Add a useEffect that reconciles message isStreaming from stream.state.isStreaming: when stream.state.isStreaming transitions to false while activeMwikilaIdRef.current is set, finalize that message (clear isStreaming, run onReceive, null the ref) so a missing turn_end can never strand the bubble.

title: Signal token ramp is non-monotonic in light mode — signal-600 (L40%) is LIGHTER than signal-500 (L38%), so primary CTAs lighten on hover instead of darkening
reason: Independently confirmed. In the light-mode :root block of packages/design-system/src/styles/globals.css, --signal-500 = '18 70% 38%' (line 94, L=38%) and --signal-600 = '22 60% 40%' (line 95, L=40%), so signal-600 is 2% LIGHTER than signal-500. The tailwind config (packages/design-system/tailwind.config.ts:82-83) maps signal.500/600 to hsl(var(--signal-500))/hsl(var(--signal-600)), so the classes resolve to those vars. The three cited consumers all use `bg-signal-500 ... hover:bg-signal-600` on guest light-first surfaces: apps/owner-portal/src/app/not-found.tsx:34 (file comment explicitly: 'Owner surface is light-first'), apps/owner-portal/src/app/error.tsx:57, apps/marketing/src/components/CookieConsent.tsx:176 and :219. In light mode the hover therefore lightens the button (38%->40%) rather than darkening it, inverting the intended press affordance. The dark-mode override (globals.css:238-239: signal-500='24 68% 58%', signal-600='28 72% 64%') is intentionally higher=lighter, so the bug is light-mode-only, exactly as claimed. Not in KNOWN_ISSUES.md (KI-001..KI-Wave18 are unrelated). Reachable in shipped guest recovery/consent surfaces.
userImpact: On light-mode guest surfaces (404 page, error/retry page, cookie-consent Accept/Save buttons) the primary copper CTA gets visibly ~2% lighter on hover instead of darker — a subtle backwards press cue on exactly the recovery/consent surfaces. Purely cosmetic; no functional or accessibility regression (both states still pass contrast against the cream canvas). Hence severity lowered from medium to low.
proposedFix: Restore light-mode ramp monotonicity: set --signal-600 darker than --signal-500 (e.g. ~16 66% 31%) and cascade 700/800/900, OR keep the AA-safe hero copper at 500 and re-point the slightly brighter accent to a dedicated --signal-450/--signal-550, leaving the 50->950 ramp strictly increasing in darkness. Then re-audit each hover:bg-signal-600 / hover:text-signal-700 call-site.
